content_preview.title: PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 Fix Two Critical Unauthenticated RCE Flaws, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619
content_preview.summary: PHP's security release names the two CVSS 9.2 flaws as CVE-2026-109618 (OOM corruption) and CVE-2026-109619 (stale global state), fixed in four branches.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The security release the PHP project [pre-announced on October 20](/article/2026-10/21-php-pre-announces-october-21-security-release-for-two-critical-vulnerabilities-rated-cvss-v40-92) shipped on October 21, 2026. According to the [PHP.net announcement](https://www.php.net/index.php), PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 "fix two critical vulnerabilities that can allow unauthenticated remote code execution." The notice says: "There are no complete mitigations, updating is the only ...

editor_notes.content_quality: Compact, well-structured Briefing (644 words, range 300-800). Clear Overview / What We Know / Who Is Exposed / Interim Mitigations / What We Don't Know structure. Appropriately technical for a developer/sysadmin audience; neutral tone, no AI self-reference.
editor_notes.source_verification: All three snapshots read from disk (gunzip; manifest status 200, no suspicious_patterns on any source, no archive fallback) and then re-verified live: advisories fetched raw via the GitHub API (repos/php/php-src/security-advisories/<GHSA>) and compared with snapshots (source-1.html.gz, source-2.html.gz). source-0.html.gz (php.net front page): confirms the 21 Oct 2026 security advisory item ('PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 fix two critical vulnerabilities that can allow unauthenticated remote code execution'), the 'no complete mitigations, updating is the only safe choice' sentence (appears in each per-branch release item, not in the advisory item - the article's 'the notice says' is acceptable), the 'all PHP installations serving web requests' list (PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP, LiteSpeed), the mod_php 'demonstrated exploit where an unauthenticated request can trigger the attack before any application code runs', PHP 8.1 and older no longer updated, 'minimal source-backports for PHP 7.4, PHP 8.0, and PHP 8.1', distro/LTS vendors received patches in advance, PHP 8.2 EOL 31 December 2026, PHP 8.6.0 RC4 (21 Oct) containing the fixes with RC5 planned for 5 November 2026, and all interim mitigations (memory_limit=-1 via php_admin_value, post_max_size 8M / 32M, do not substitute RLIMIT_AS/RLIMIT_DATA, session.upload_progress.enabled=0 + restart workers, fatal_error_backtraces=0 on PHP 8.5, 'reduce exposure to specific attack paths but do not make an installation safe'). source-1 (GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w) via API: CVE-2026-109618, summary 'RCE via OOM corruption', severity critical, CVSS v4.0 score 9.2, vector CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N (no CVSS v3 score), CWE-416/755/824/1325/1419, vulnerable <8.2.35, <8.3.36, <8.4.27, <8.5.12 with those four patched versions, published 2026-10-21T13:34:25Z, reporters lcfr-hax, sagitzadik-wiz, tomash-areion, amyb-oai (not named in the article). Quotes verified verbatim: 'PHP uses longjmp() for out-of-memory (OOM) errors', 'unconditionally invokes the request shutdown procedure, even when request startup has failed', 'FPM exits the child when request startup fails', 'no complete FPM exploit has been demonstrated for this SAPI', 'was validated over HTTP against mod_php with default PHP input and memory limits', exploit portability/reliability depends on build, extensions, frontend behavior and allocator layout. source-2 (GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp): CVE-2026-109619, 'RCE via stale global state', critical, identical CVSS v4.0 9.2 vector, same CWEs, same affected/patched versions, published 2026-10-21T13:34:13Z, same reporters. Quotes verified: 'The demonstrated producing and consuming operations occur in different HTTP requests handled by the same worker', 'the strongest demonstrated case' (PHP 8.5 fatal error backtrace, basis of confirmed mod_php exploitation), session upload progress lifecycle confirmed, 'does not protect against this vulnerability' for error_reporting/@/display_errors/log_errors. 'Unauthenticated' is NOT the writer's inference: the OOM advisory states 'The confirmed impact is unauthenticated remote code execution as the web worker account', the stale-state advisory says 'unauthenticated heap use-after-free, memory disclosure and remote code execution', the vector has PR:N, and php.net uses the phrase. The title's 'Unauthenticated RCE' is supported. github.com and php.net are both on the allowlist (php.net added in the previous batch).
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every number, version, date, CVE id, GHSA id, quote and attribution traced to a snapshot or the live API. Article says 'CVSS score of 9.2' without naming the version; the advisories use CVSS v4.0 (the linked earlier article states v4.0) - not an error, the label could have been explicit. 'October 20' pre-announcement date matches the notice date (20 Oct) in the earlier article. No claim of exploitation in the wild; the article states the sources do not say, which is accurate (neither advisory nor php.net says either way; php.net says only 'demonstrated exploit' for mod_php). Does not repeat the unsourced LWN reader-comment claims about AI-assisted pre-embargo disclosure; the submission contains no mention of LWN. Credits not mentioned, which is acceptable.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral, attributed, no sensationalism. 'Critical' and 'unauthenticated' are the sources' own terms.
editor_notes.originality: Justified follow-up to the published Briefing '21-php-pre-announces-october-21-security-release...' (internal link /article/2026-10/21-php-pre-announces-october-21-security-release-for-two-critical-vulnerabilities-rated-cvss-v40-92 resolves to an existing article file and is described accurately: pre-announcement of an Oct 21 release). That article explicitly listed CVE ids, names, affected components and branches as unknown; this one supplies them from the release and advisories, so it is a genuine development, not a duplicate.
concerns: Minor: the CVSS version (v4.0) is not named in the body, only 'CVSS score of 9.2'; not a factual error.

Minor: 'There are no complete mitigations, updating is the only safe choice' is quoted as from 'the notice' but appears in the per-branch release items on the same page rather than in the security-advisory item.
recommendations: Name the CVSS version (v4.0) explicitly in future vulnerability coverage.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-sourced follow-up with all specifics verified against the raw advisories and the php.net front page; no corrections needed. Integrity checks, signature and word count pass; no suspicious_patterns; no orphan or missing source URLs. Featured candidacy: 3 - two demonstrated unauthenticated RCE flaws (CVSS v4.0 9.2) in PHP, which runs a large share of the web, with no complete mitigation short of updating
